hints.title: Weight Contribution Analysis
hints.text: Consider which pizzas contribute to your weight on odd days compared to even days.

hints.title: Odd versus Even Days
hints.text: On odd days, you receive the single largest pizza in the group. On even days, you receive the second largest pizza.

hints.title: Greedy Descending Allocation
hints.text: Sort the array descending. Take the first (total_days + 1) // 2 largest pizzas for the odd days. For even days, pair each scored pizza with an available larger pizza.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxWeight(self, pizzas: list[int]) -> int:
        pizzas.sort(reverse=True)
        total_days = len(pizzas) // 4
        odd_days = (total_days + 1) // 2
        even_days = total_days // 2
        ans = 0
        for i in range(odd_days):
            ans += pizzas[i]
        idx = odd_days
        for _ in range(even_days):
            idx += 1
            ans += pizzas[idx]
            idx += 1
        return ans
```

variables: n: number of pizzas in the input array
complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(n log n) time followed by an O(n / 4) traversal to aggregate weights.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all partitions of pizzas into groups of 4 leads to combinatorial explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting allows immediate greedy selection of optimal pizza weights.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize the difference in selection between odd and even days and apply greedy ordering.
